target.title: feat(ui): surface still-running background tasks after the chat turn settles
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106107.

When an agent turn finishes while background tasks (subagents) are still running, the chat goes quiet: the working claw disappears and the only remaining signal is the small badge on the tasks-rail toggle. It is easy to miss that work is still happening, there is no glanceable elapsed time, and no one-click path from the conversation to the running task.

## Why This Change Was Made

After the turn settles, while the pane's agent still has queued/running tasks, the thread now shows a compact status row right above the composer:

- the claw glyph, parked slightly nose-down (the combo animation's cross pose), static — no shadowboxing back-and-forth, only a slow opacity breath (disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`)
- a live elapsed label (`openclaw-elapsed-time`, oldest active task start) with `tabular-nums` so the ticking digits do not shift the row
- a "1 running task" / "{count} running tasks" link that opens the background-tasks rail

The row hides while the agent is visibly working (`runWorking` — the working claw owns that state), on the empty/welcome thread, and disappears when the last task finishes. It reuses the tasks-rail snapshot already loaded by the chat pane (`tasks.list` + live `task` events), so there is no new polling or RPC.

Implementation: `activeBackgroundTasksStatus` + `renderBackgroundTasksStatusRow` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-background-tasks.ts`, rendered at the bottom of `renderChatThread` (outside the `guard()` memo so the ticker stays live), `backgroundTasks` prop threaded through `chat-view.ts`. New i18n keys `chat.backgroundTasks.statusRunningOne/statusRunningMany` (en.ts only, per locale pipeline). The mock dev harness gained a running-task fixture so the row, rail, and badge are demoable.

## User Impact

Operators see at a glance that their agent still has background work running after the reply lands — with elapsed time and a direct link to the task list — while the composer stays free to keep talking to the agent.

![status row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/running-tasks-status-row/tasks-status-row.png)

Clicking the link opens the tasks rail:

![rail open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/running-tasks-status-row/tasks-status-rail-open.png)

## Evidence

- Focused tests on Blacksmith Testbox (`tbx_01kxd2ah0zg5qkjhjr548bhm65`): `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-background-tasks.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts` → 2 files, 199 tests passed (includes new coverage: status summary math, render/link behavior, plural label, suppression while `runWorking`).
- Live verification against `pnpm dev:ui:mock`: row renders after the settled turn, ticks (55s → 1m 5s …) without horizontal jitter (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` computed), claw static at `rotate(8deg)` with jaw at `rotate(-4deg)` and only the `chatTasksStatusBreath` opacity animation; clicking "1 running task" opens the Background tasks rail showing the running subagent.
- `pnpm check:changed` delegated to the same Testbox lease: conflict-marker lane green; the TypeScript LOC ratchet flagged the four grown >500-LOC files, resolved by recording the growth in `scripts/ts-max-loc-baseline-v2.json` (the reviewable-growth artifact from #105952) — net +284 test-inclusive LOC is feature surface, not refactor drift. `node scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --max 500` passes on the committed tree.
- oxfmt clean on all touched files.
